title: Bayer CropScience Declares ₹90 Interim Dividend: What It Means
description: Bayer CropScience has announced an interim dividend of ₹90 per equity share for the financial year 2026-27. This dividend translates to a 900% payout based on.

faq.a: An interim dividend is a dividend declared and paid by a company during its ongoing financial year, before the final annual results are announced. It's typically based on the company's performance during a specific quarter or half-year period.

The 900% payout is calculated based on the face value of the share, not its market price. If the face value of Bayer CropScience shares is ₹10, then a 900% payout means 900% of ₹10, which equals ₹90 per share.

faq.q: What is the significance of the record date?
faq.a: The record date (November 12, 2026, for this dividend) is the cut-off date set by the company to determine which shareholders are eligible to receive the dividend. Only those who hold the shares in their demat account by the end of this date will receive the dividend.

faq.q: Is dividend income taxable in India?
faq.a: Yes, dividend income received by individual shareholders is fully taxable in India. It is added to your total income and taxed at your applicable income tax slab rates.

faq.q: Will TDS be deducted on this dividend?
faq.a: Yes, if the dividend amount you receive from Bayer CropScience exceeds ₹5,000 in a financial year, the company is mandated to deduct Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) at 10% (if PAN is provided).
